query_text: where does the sound come from when you crack your knuckles

content.text:
The “crack” sound from cracking your knuckles mostly comes from **gas bubbles rapidly forming and changing inside the synovial fluid** of the joint.

Your knuckle joints are surrounded by a capsule filled with **synovial fluid**, which lubricates the joint. When you pull or bend the joint, you increase the space inside the joint capsule, which **drops the pressure** in the fluid. Dissolved gases—mainly carbon dioxide—come out of solution and form a bubble or cavity. That rapid change creates the popping sound.

This process is called **cavitation**.

Afterward, it usually takes a while before you can crack the same knuckle again because the gases need time to dissolve back into the fluid and the joint has to reset.

And despite the common myth, ordinary knuckle cracking has **not been clearly shown to cause arthritis**, though it can irritate soft tissues if done aggressively or painfully.
